entities.summary: Walter of Winterburn was a prominent English Dominican cardinal, orator, poet, philosopher, and theologian who played a significant role in shaping medieval religious thought. Born in unknown circumstances, Walter rose to prominence in the late 13th century as a leading voice in the Dominican Order. He was a prolific writer and speaker, and his works had a lasting impact on the development of scholastic theology. In 1305, Walter died, leaving behind a legacy that continued to influence religious debates in Europe for centuries to come. He is remembered as a key figure in the transmission of Aristotelian thought and the development of Dominican spirituality. Walter's writings on theology and philosophy have been studied by scholars for centuries, and his influence can still be seen in modern Catholic doctrine. Through his writings and teachings, Walter helped to shape the intellectual landscape of medieval Europe, leaving a lasting impact on the development of Western civilization.
